links.note: Machine-readable transcription of PROTOCOL.md, which was committed and pushed in bd5d146b before any held-out split count was computed. This JSON was written after the held-out run, on review (Codex P1, PR #2736); it transcribes PROTOCOL.md and adds no test, threshold or population, so freeze.filed_before_affected_data is false. PROTOCOL.md's count typo (48 for 42 held-out curves in the four fields; 48 includes P-384) is recorded post-run in AMENDMENT.md and changes no cell. heldout.py was written after PROTOCOL.md was pushed and before it ran, but was not hash-frozen before data.

question: Among prime-order draft-eligible curves in the recovered NIST/ANSI seed streams, do the published curves have lower small-prime split counts (odd l <= 691 with t^2-4p a nonzero square mod l) than unpublished curves of the same field that were not among the eleven named omissions?

claims.text: Each split count is an exact Legendre-symbol computation on archived p and certified prime n.
Published curves have lower split counts than held-out unpublished eligible curves of the same field (association replicates outside the named eleven).
claims.if_supported: a label association on these streams only; no ECDLP weakness, mechanism or intent
claims.if_not_supported: the published-low association seen on the named nineteen does not replicate on held-out curves

hypotheses.statement: Published curves were selected (deliberately or as a side effect) for few split small primes.
hypotheses.mechanism: none known; split primes are Elkies primes (rational l-isogenies), with no known effect on ECDLP cost

data_seen.measured: split counts of the nineteen named curves (exploratory; motivates this test)

arms.description: eight published same-field curves (prime192v1-v3, secp224r1, prime239v1-v3, prime256v1); P-384 published descriptive only
42 unpublished draft-eligible positions labelled order_too_wide_only or opposite_root_only in the 192/224/239/256-bit fields (6 more in P-384, descriptive)
the eleven named omissions; exploratory population, secondary comparison only
analytic prime-order Chebotarev null for each field (no rows; exact Poisson-binomial law)

aa.not_applicable_reason: split counts are exact, deterministic arithmetic with no measurement noise; the noise floor of the label comparison is the within-field label-permutation null, which is the test itself

positive.not_applicable_reason: not run; the Legendre-symbol instrument was independently verified on the nineteen named curves by the prior Sage check (sea_signature verification.json), and the permutation test detects the nineteen-curve association at p = 0.0002 at B = 691 (runs/permute.json), but no planted-effect arm was constructed for the held-out population

null_population.description: prime-order curves over the same field under the Chebotarev model: Frobenius mod l uniform on GL2(F_l) with det p and no eigenvalue 1, independent over l; exact Poisson-binomial law per field
null_population.generator: analysis_lib.probs / pmf (exact); validated against PARI SEA counts at 48 bits (runs/validation48_stdout.log)
null_population.why_n: held-out percentiles of all 42 eligible positions compared with uniform (secondary 1)

factors.name: cutoff_B
factors.how: frozen in PROTOCOL.md; other cutoffs sensitivity only

factors.name: root_branch
factors.how: both square-root branches share Delta (isomorphic or quadratic twist); asserted per position

factors.name: order_bit_width
factors.how: order_too_wide_only positions differ from the named eleven in order width; recorded per row as kind

comparisons.reason: the named eleven were picked retrospectively by a root/bit-width screen and were the exploratory sample that motivated the statistic; descriptive only

randomization.arm_order_reason: exact arithmetic, order cannot affect a Legendre symbol

instance_sampling.rule: all positions with the named labels in nist_seed_1997_acceptance_20261024/analysis.json; no sampling

blinding.how: not masked: labels define the test; statistic and population fixed before data

power.note: 102 within-field pairs (8 published x 42 held-out by field); fixed by the archive, not chosen for power. Resolution 2/(N+1) ~ 1e-5 << 0.05. No effect-size power claim.

preflight_runtime.measured_on: exploratory analysis.py on the same host (7 s)

primary.name: held-out over published pair fraction
primary.definition: over all within-field (held-out, published) pairs in the four fields, fraction with split(held-out) > split(published), ties 1/2; uncertainty is the one-sided within-field label-permutation p-value (200,000 draws, seed 20261029)
primary.formula: sum over fields f, sum over (h in heldout_f, q in published_f) of [S_h > S_q] + 0.5[S_h = S_q], divided by the number of such pairs (102)

secondary.name: null mid-percentile
secondary.definition: 100*(P(X<S)+P(X=S)/2) under the field's prime-order Poisson-binomial null
secondary.formula: 100 * (sum_{k<S} pmf_f(k) + pmf_f(S)/2), pmf_f the Poisson-binomial law with P_l^split from analysis_lib.probs(p_f, l)

stopping_rules.rule: fixed population: every labelled position, one pass

invalidation_rules: a position missing a certificate, with uncertified or non-prime n, or whose branches disagree on Delta fails the run closed

decision_rule.text: C2 replicates if the one-sided within-field label-permutation p of pair_fraction is <= 0.05; otherwise it does not replicate.

inadmissible: choosing a different cutoff, ramified convention or population after seeing held-out results
reading the sensitivity cutoffs as tests
reading a label association as an ECDLP weakness

literature.claim: 69 draft-eligible certified prime-order seed positions and their labels
